Berestechko Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Berestechko, Ukraine

Demolished. Most likely founded alongside the community's emergence in the late 16th century, this cemetery appeared on maps by the mid-19th century and was finally destroyed in 1952. Jews settled in Berestechko from the mid-16th century; population reached 50 by 1577 and 1,050 by 1648, before the Khmelnytsky massacre killed 200 families, leaving only 12 Jewish houses standing. By the second half of the 18th century, plague killed all but five shtetl residents. Growth resumed as the town became a Russian-Austrian trade transit point; population reached 2,251 by 1897, with four synagogues by century's end (two belonging to the Olyka and Trisk Hasidic movements). A 1901 Jewish vocational school for men (led by I. Kagan), poorhouse, and library preceded early 20th-century Bund and Zionist youth organizations. A Hebrew school and library opened in 1918, followed by a 1930 Jewish national bank; population reached 2,625 by 1937. Wehrmacht occupation from June 24, 1941 to April 2, 1944 began with a August 8, 1941 Aktion killing 300 Jews; an October 1941 ghetto absorbed Jews from surrounding villages before its liquidation on September 7-9, 1942, when 3,000 Jews were shot. A 1990 monument marks the execution site.
